name: har2client
alternateName: har2client: from recorded API traffic to a working client
description: A benchmark of tasks in which a model reads a goal and a recording of API traffic (HAR) and writes a Python client that must work on a fresh copy of the API. Hidden execution tests are kept outside the dataset; rebuilding them needs the benchmark code, which is public at https://github.com/MohitGoyal09/har2client. Configs: tier_a (27 public-API tasks; 30 were built and run, and 3 whose API spec has a restrictive licence are not published) and tier_b (50 invented stateful-API tasks), which are case 1 (build); and heal_v3 and heal_v3_hint, the case 3 (maintain) v3 evaluation suite: 64 repair tasks (single 14, release3 10, release4 8, partial 8, sdk 8, misleading 8, terse 8), each in two arms (as built, and with a contract hint paragraph in the goal). Case 2 (probe) and the earlier case 3 sets (v2) are not in this release.
citeAs: @misc{har2client2026, title={har2client: a benchmark and environment for turning recorded API traffic into working clients}, author={Mohit Goyal and Ananya Bhattacharya}, year={2026}, url={https://huggingface.co/datasets/ORG/har2client}}

rai:dataLimitations: Controlled stateful APIs: Tier B comes from one engine with six feature switches, not from real services. All traffic is synthetic. Tier A covers OpenAPI 3.0 specs from APIs.guru only and 27 published tasks from the 165 selected APIs (30 were built and run; the 3 with a restrictive spec licence are not published, and the Tier A results include them). Case 3 v3 comes from the same invented engine with ten API changes (five silent wire changes and five protocol changes), so it tests those changes, not real service releases. Pass rates are one run per task so far. Tier A is nearly saturated and may be partly memorised. Hidden tests are not in this dataset; rebuilding them needs the benchmark code, which is public at https://github.com/MohitGoyal09/har2client.
rai:dataBiases: Selection bias: Tier A keeps public APIs with OpenAPI 3.0 specs, 5 to 40 operations, JSON bodies and at most 2 per provider, so it over-represents well documented REST APIs. Tier B domains (invoices, samples, bookings, tickets, shipments) and feature switches are chosen by us. Goal argument names often equal wire names, which favours string matching. Text is English only.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: None. Recordings are synthetic; credentials, tokens and user names are generated fake strings; data values are random or invented. Tier A uses real API titles and operation names but no real user data.
rai:dataUseCases: Evaluating models and agents on traffic-to-client generation with execution-based grading; studying which API behaviours cause failures; training and evaluating RL agents with the environment in the benchmark code (https://github.com/MohitGoyal09/har2client). Not for measuring general coding ability, real-world reverse-engineering success, or security capability.
rai:dataSocialImpact: Lower risk: all servers and credentials are fake, and the task is to write a client for a known API. Possible benefit: better tooling for integrating undocumented APIs. Possible misuse: teaching systems to replicate client behaviour of real services; the data contains no real credentials or endpoints to attack. Benchmark scores can be over-read; the card lists caveats.
rai:dataCollection: Generated by code. Tier A: an APIs.guru OpenAPI 3.0 spec drives a fake server; a scripted user plays 1 to 3 calls per operation (up to 8 operations); the session is recorded as a HAR and mixed with simulated browser noise (70% of entries). Tier B: one stateful engine with six switches builds invented APIs. Case 3 (v3): the same engine builds a v1 and a v2 version of an invented API; a release of 1, 3 or 4 changes turns v1 into v2; the task holds the v1 client, a failure log from a practice server, a short recording of v2 (with noise 0.3) and, for 8 tasks, release notes with one wrong statement. Seeds 2001 to 2064 (build seed 2); the list was frozen in the pre-registration before the first run.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: HAR recordings are mixed with simulated noise (analytics, fonts, CDN assets, same-origin XHR) using one shared browser header profile. The export copies the visible goal and recording unchanged and drops all hidden files.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: No human annotation. Hidden tests are generated by code from seeds; each task is valid only if the reference client scores 1.0.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: har2client task builder, reference-client generator and grader (benchmark code, https://github.com/MohitGoyal09/har2client)
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: Case 2 will be added as a new config. The v3 case 3 results (more efforts, repeat runs) will be added as they finish. Task changes get a new version tag. Tier B can be regenerated with new seeds for a fresh private split. Feedback through Hub discussions.
